Driving a truck requires physical work. Physical changes -- products, manufacture, and the inevitable regulation -- take time. Pure intelligence jobs are easier to replace by software, hence coding and maths are among the first to have AI as serious competitors. 

Next up will be a lot of academic disciplines, from theoretical physics to economics. We can already see this beginning now.

There must be a lot of scientific discoveries hidden in the scientific literature, conclusions that have not been drawn simply because no human has been able to read everything that has been published. AI is about to pick those fruits in the coming year ringing in what might be akin a second scientific revolution. This is going to keep the stock market excited for some time. 

I also expect, unfortunately, that the models which are most capable at scientific discovery will be increasingly restricted to members of institutions that have made deals with the leading companies. (Which isn't going to end well for the EU.)

As usual, you shouldn't believe a word I say because as everyone will tell you, I don't know anything about nothing. But at least I have consistently said the same thing for a few years now.

urls.description: This dataset provides global Groundwater Storage Change (GWSC) expressed as storage anomalies on a 0.5° regular grid. The dataset provides a value of groundwater storage change in mm equivalent water height and its uncertainty for each grid cell. The dataset is part of the Essential Climate Variable (ECV) Service called Terrestrial Water Storage and Groundwater, comprising of ECV Products for Terrestrial Water Storage Anomalies (TWSA) and GWSC. The data represents the currently only available technology to measure changes in groundwater storage on a global scale. The dataset is a Level-4 product (compare section 1.1.2.1. in the Product User Guide and Specification (PUGS)) that provides groundwater storage change as mm equivalent water height on a regular grid. Input datasets are (Level-3) terrestrial water storage and global datasets on water storage change derived from glacier mass, snow cover, root zone soil moisture and surface water. Meta has already deployed millions of AMD EPYC processors, including those powering its Muse AI agent, while Instinct GPUs are being used in production for AI training, ranking, and recommendation workloads.

Looking ahead, Meta plans to deploy a custom MI450-based Instinct GPU optimized for its workloads and is a lead customer for AMD's 6th Gen EPYC processors.

The companies are also expanding software collaboration across ROCm and PyTorch, building on their previously announced 6-gigawatt AMD GPU agreement.

note_tweet.text:
Ask The Chain About The Threat.

Quantum risk is usually a headline. On QuanChain it is a number you can query.

Every node exposes the oracle over JSON-RPC.

⚛️ oracle_getQuantumThreatLevel returns the current threat level, from 0 to 6. oracle_getLQCpH returns the live reading of the cost per logical qubit-hour.

⚛️ oracle_getSecurityRecommendation takes a value and returns the security level recommended for it. oracle_getBreakCost estimates the cost to break a given algorithm.

⚛️ oracle_getHistory returns past readings between any two points.

A wallet, an exchange or a researcher can ask the chain what it thinks the threat is today, and see how that answer has moved.
